issues.legal_issue: A court retains discretion not to strike a defendant’s defence for default in depositing rent even when the defendant made no timely representation.
material_facts: A lessor sued to evict a lessee and recover rent arrears.
During the suit, the lessee failed to make regular deposits of monthly rent.
The lessee made no representation within the prescribed time opposing the striking of the defence.
The trial court struck the defence, and the High Court affirmed on the basis that the court had no discretion to do otherwise.
The Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s order and remanded the case for fresh consideration.
issues.conclusion: A court is not obliged to strike off the defence in every case of default, even if the defendant made no timely representation; it retains discretion to decline to do so when the material on the record provides good reason. The appeal was allowed and the case remanded for fresh consideration.
issues.legal_principle: Order XV Rule 5(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, as re-enacted by the U.P. Civil Laws (Amendment) Act 1976, uses the word “may” and gives the court power, not an obligation, to strike off the defence for deposit default. Under Rule 5(2), the court must consider a timely representation, but the absence of one does not eliminate the court’s discretion to consider material already on the record. Because striking off the defence is penal, the power must not be exercised mechanically. The Court disagreed with and overruled the contrary view in Puran Chand v. Pravin Gupta.

predicates.eviction_rent_suit: A lessor brought a suit seeking eviction of a lessee and recovery of rent or compensation.
predicates.rent_deposit_default: The defendant failed to make a required deposit of rent during the suit.
predicates.no_timely_representation: The defendant did not make a representation opposing the striking of the defence within the prescribed time.
predicates.court_retains_discretion_not_to_strike_d: The court has discretion to decline to strike the defence when the material before it provides good reason.

issues.definition: When a lessor’s eviction-and-rent suit involves a deposit default and no timely representation, the court nevertheless retains discretion not to strike the defence.
